reconcile.note: Clarke reads the eleven's exclamation as tentative conjecture from Peter's return, not confirmed faith, consistent with Mark's report they still disbelieved the Emmaus pair.

discrepancy.note: Strauss flags the plain clash: Luke has the assembled disciples already greeting the Emmaus pair with belief, while Mark has them remain incredulous.

quotes.text: the contradiction, that while in Luke the assembled disciples meet those coming from Emmaus with the believing exclamation: the Lord is risen, etc., in Mark the disciples are said to have remained incredulous even to the account of those two witnesses, probably proceeds from nothing more than an exaggeration of Mark
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), on Mark 16:13 and Luke 24:34.

sides.snippet: They went away and told it to the rest. They didn't believe them, either.
sides.verseText: They went away and told it to the rest. They didn't believe them, either.

sides.snippet: The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!
sides.verseText: saying, \"The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!\"
